questions.stem: Which of the following best describes an office?
options: A place where raw materials are turned into finished goods for sale to the public
A room used only for storing spare equipment
A place where information is received, recorded, processed and given out
A section of a factory where machines are repaired
A shop where goods are displayed for sale to customers
questions.explanation: The office handles information for the organisation.

questions.stem: Which of these is a function of a modern office?
options: Manufacturing products for export to neighbouring countries
questions.explanation: Receiving, recording, arranging and giving out information are office functions.

questions.stem: In the head office of a Lagos insurance firm, forty clerks sit at desks in one big hall with no partitions, while their supervisor sits at the end of the hall. This layout is
questions.explanation: Open-plan offices place staff together in one large space.

questions.stem: Which is an advantage of a closed (private) office over an open-plan office?
options: It makes supervision of many staff easier
It gives privacy for confidential work and discussions
It is cheaper to heat, light and clean than shared open spaces
It allows easy sharing of equipment
It encourages constant movement of staff
questions.explanation: Private offices give privacy and reduce noise and distraction.

questions.stem: The office that controls all the activities of a company from one central location is the
questions.explanation: Head office directs the whole organisation.

questions.stem: Kemi works from her home in Ibadan using a laptop, Internet connection and video calls, sending reports to her company in Lagos. This arrangement is best described as
questions.explanation: Working remotely with ICT links is teleworking.

questions.stem: Centralisation of office services, such as having one typing and printing pool for all departments, has the advantage that
options: each department gets a totally private and personal typing service of its own
work is never delayed at busy periods
departmental managers can supervise the typists directly
equipment and specialist staff are fully used, reducing cost
confidential documents are always kept within departments
questions.explanation: Centralisation allows better use of staff and machines and lower costs.

questions.stem: Which department in a company is responsible for recruiting and training staff?
questions.explanation: Personnel/HR handles recruitment, training and welfare.

questions.stem: The department that keeps the financial records and pays salaries is the
questions.explanation: Accounts handles financial records and payroll.

questions.stem: The department that buys raw materials and office supplies at the best price and quality is the
questions.explanation: Purchasing (procurement) buys the organisation's requirements.

questions.stem: Which department would most likely handle a customer's complaint about a newspaper report damaging the company's image?
questions.explanation: PR manages the organisation's image and relations with the public.

questions.stem: In an organisation chart, a line of authority running directly from the managing director down to junior staff shows
questions.explanation: Line organisation shows direct chain of command.

questions.stem: The principle that each worker should take orders from only one superior is called
questions.explanation: Unity of command avoids conflicting instructions.

questions.stem: A supervisor directly controls 25 clerks and finds it difficult to give each enough attention. The problem relates to
options: the chain of command being too short
span of control being too wide
questions.explanation: Span of control is the number of subordinates a superior controls.

questions.stem: Which machine is used to produce exact copies of a document on paper quickly?
questions.explanation: Photocopiers reproduce documents.

questions.stem: A paper shredder is used to
questions.explanation: Shredders cut documents into strips for secure disposal.

questions.stem: The machine that prints postage impressions on envelopes so that stamps need not be used is the
questions.explanation: Franking machines print paid postage marks.

questions.stem: Which machine arranges the pages of a multi-page document in the correct order?
questions.explanation: Collators sort sheets into sets in page order.

questions.stem: A laminating machine is used to
options: cut large sheets of paper into small pieces of equal size for notepads
punch holes in paper for filing
cover documents such as identity cards with a protective plastic film
questions.explanation: Lamination seals documents in plastic.

questions.stem: Which factor is LEAST important when an office manager is choosing a new photocopier?
options: The volume of copies needed each month
The colour of the delivery van of the supplier
The cost of buying and maintaining the machine
The space available in the office
questions.explanation: Choice depends on workload, cost, service and space, not irrelevant factors.

questions.stem: An organisation prefers to lease rather than buy expensive office machines mainly because leasing
options: always makes the organisation the legal owner of the machine from the very first day
is free of any regular payment
gives the machines a longer life
avoids a large initial capital outlay and often includes maintenance
removes the need for staff training
questions.explanation: Leasing spreads cost and frequently includes servicing.

questions.stem: When a stranger walks into a company building for the first time, the person he normally meets before anyone else works at the
questions.explanation: The receptionist receives visitors first.

questions.stem: The book in which the receptionist writes the names of visitors and the times they arrive and leave is the
questions.explanation: The visitors' register records callers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a quality of a good receptionist?
options: Leaving the desk unattended for long periods
questions.explanation: Courtesy creates a good first impression.

questions.stem: A receptionist keeps a list of appointments made for the managers. This record is the
questions.explanation: An appointments diary records booked meetings.

questions.stem: A visitor without an appointment insists on seeing the managing director, who is in a meeting. The receptionist should
options: allow the visitor into the meeting room at once
ask the visitor to leave immediately
politely explain the situation and offer an appointment or another officer
ignore the visitor until he goes away
tell the visitor that the director has resigned and will not return to the office
questions.explanation: Tact and courtesy with an alternative are expected.

questions.stem: A business card handed to a receptionist by a visitor is useful mainly because it
options: serves as a receipt for payment
replaces the need for an appointment with any officer of the organisation
acts as a pass to enter any office
shows the visitor's date of birth
gives the visitor's name, position and contact details accurately
questions.explanation: It gives accurate details for records and introductions.

questions.stem: A document that requests a supplier to supply goods is a
questions.explanation: Orders request goods from suppliers.

questions.stem: The document given as evidence that money has been paid is a
questions.explanation: A receipt acknowledges payment.

questions.stem: A document sent by a seller informing the buyer that goods have been dispatched and are on their way is the
questions.explanation: An advice note tells the buyer goods are coming.

questions.stem: A summary sent to a customer at the end of the month showing transactions and the balance owed is the
questions.explanation: Statements show the month's transactions and balance.

questions.stem: A seller who has undercharged a customer will correct the mistake by issuing a
questions.explanation: A debit note increases the amount the buyer owes.

questions.stem: A pro forma invoice is mostly used when
options: the goods are returned as faulty
the seller wants to cancel a sale that was agreed by telephone
the buyer must pay before the goods are dispatched
goods are being stored in a warehouse
questions.explanation: Pro forma invoices request payment in advance or serve as quotations.

questions.stem: Which document must the buyer's storekeeper sign to confirm that goods have been received in good condition?
questions.explanation: The delivery note is signed on receipt of goods.

questions.stem: The Accounts Manager wants to remind all heads of department, in writing, to submit their budgets by Friday. The most suitable document is a
questions.explanation: Memos are internal communications.

questions.stem: In a business letter, "Yours faithfully" is used with the salutation
questions.explanation: Formal impersonal salutations go with Yours faithfully.

questions.stem: The part of a business letter that shows the main subject in one line just after the salutation is the
questions.explanation: The subject heading summarises the letter's topic.

questions.stem: The letters "Encl." at the bottom of a business letter show that
options: the letter has been copied to others
something has been attached to the letter
the letter has been signed by an assistant
questions.explanation: Encl. indicates enclosures.

questions.stem: A letter sent to many customers informing them of a change of company address is a
questions.explanation: Circulars carry the same message to many readers.

questions.stem: The letters "c.c." at the foot of a letter followed by names indicate that
options: copies of the letter have been sent to those named
the named people must reply at once
the letter was typed by those named
the named people should pay the bill
the letter is to be filed under the names of those people only
questions.explanation: c.c. lists recipients of copies.

questions.stem: The style of letter layout in which every line, including the date and complimentary close, starts at the left margin is the
questions.explanation: Fully blocked layout aligns all lines at the left margin.

questions.stem: The section of an office that receives, sorts and sends out letters is the
questions.explanation: The mail room handles incoming and outgoing mail.

questions.stem: When opening incoming mail, a clerk stamps each letter with the date it was received using a
questions.explanation: A date stamp records the date of receipt.

questions.stem: A book in which a mail clerk records money and cheques found in incoming letters is the
questions.explanation: Remittances received are recorded for control.

questions.stem: Letters marked "Private" or "Confidential" should be
options: opened and read by the mail clerk
sent to the filing clerk first
questions.explanation: Confidential mail goes unopened to the named person.

questions.stem: The book used to record the cost of stamps bought and used for outgoing letters is the
questions.explanation: The postage book controls stamp use.

questions.stem: A clerk finds that a letter mentions an enclosure which is missing. The correct action is to
options: note the omission on the letter and inform the sender
file the letter without telling anyone
questions.explanation: Missing enclosures are noted and reported to the sender.

questions.stem: A document must reach a client in Abuja the next morning with proof of delivery. The most suitable service is
questions.explanation: Courier services offer fast, tracked delivery with proof.

questions.stem: Filing is the process of
options: printing many copies of a document
classifying, arranging and storing documents so they can be found easily
questions.explanation: Filing stores documents systematically for retrieval.

questions.stem: Arranging files in order of customers' surnames is the
questions.explanation: Alphabetical filing uses names.

questions.stem: A company with branches in many states arranges its sales files by state and town. This method is
questions.explanation: Geographical filing groups by location.

questions.stem: Within a customer's file, letters are placed with the most recent on top. This order is
questions.explanation: Chronological order follows dates.

questions.stem: The card or slip put in place of a file that has been borrowed, showing who took it and when, is the
questions.explanation: An out guide records the borrower of a file.

questions.stem: Numerical filing needs an additional alphabetical index because
options: numbers cannot be written clearly on the covers of file folders
it is impossible to expand numerical files
users usually remember names rather than file numbers
it stops files from being borrowed
questions.explanation: The index links names to file numbers.

questions.stem: Which filing system stores folders hanging from metal rails inside a drawer so that they do not sag?
questions.explanation: Suspension filing hangs folders on rails.

questions.stem: Which of these best defines communication in an organisation?
options: transfer of information or ideas from a sender to a receiver
typing of letters in an office
questions.explanation: Communication passes information from sender to receiver.

questions.stem: A telephone call between two officers is an example of
questions.explanation: Spoken messages are oral communication.

questions.stem: Communication from a manager to the staff under him is described as
questions.explanation: Downward communication flows from superiors to subordinates.

questions.stem: The unofficial spreading of information among workers by word of mouth is called
questions.explanation: The grapevine is informal communication.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a barrier to effective communication?
options: Use of technical jargon the receiver does not understand
questions.explanation: Jargon unfamiliar to the receiver blocks understanding.

questions.stem: Charts, graphs and diagrams used to present sales figures at a meeting are examples of
questions.explanation: Information shown in pictures and charts is visual communication.

questions.stem: Feedback is important in communication mainly because it
options: shows whether the receiver has understood the message
prevents the use of written messages
removes the need for a sender
guarantees that the message will be kept secret from all other members of staff
questions.explanation: Feedback confirms understanding.

questions.stem: After the staff welfare committee met, the secretary prepared an official account of decisions taken, to be confirmed at the next meeting. This document is the
questions.explanation: Minutes record proceedings and decisions.

questions.stem: The document circulated before a meeting showing, in order, the business to be dealt with is the
questions.explanation: The agenda sets out the business to be discussed.

questions.stem: A club constitution says business may be transacted only if at least 15 members are present. This required number is known as the
questions.explanation: A quorum makes the meeting valid.

questions.stem: A formal proposal put before a meeting for discussion and voting is a
questions.explanation: A motion becomes a resolution if passed.

questions.stem: Where votes are equal, the chairman may use his
questions.explanation: The chairman's casting vote breaks a tie.

questions.stem: A shareholder who cannot attend an annual general meeting authorises another person to vote for him. The person is a
questions.explanation: A proxy votes on behalf of an absent member.

questions.stem: A meeting held once a year by a company at which accounts are presented and directors elected is the
questions.explanation: The AGM is the yearly statutory meeting of members.

questions.stem: A report is best described as
options: a list of visitors to an office
a formal account of facts or findings presented to a person or body
an advertisement placed in a newspaper for a vacancy in the organisation
questions.explanation: Reports present facts, findings and recommendations.

questions.stem: The section of a report that states the suggestions made by the writer for action is the
questions.explanation: Recommendations propose action.

questions.stem: The part of a report that states what the writer was asked to investigate is the
questions.explanation: Terms of reference define the scope of the report.

questions.stem: A report submitted at fixed intervals, such as a monthly sales report, is a
questions.explanation: Routine reports are produced regularly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a quality of a good report?
options: It contains the writer's gossip and rumours
It is as long as possible regardless of content
It is accurate, objective and clearly arranged
questions.explanation: Good reports are accurate, objective, clear and concise.

questions.stem: Detailed tables and statistics that support a report but would interrupt the main text are placed in the
questions.explanation: Supporting material goes in the appendices.

questions.stem: Information that is accurate, complete and available when needed is described as
questions.explanation: Quality information is accurate, complete and timely.

questions.stem: Which of these is a source of internal information for an organisation?
questions.explanation: Internal sources are the organisation's own records.

questions.stem: Information on the Internet, in newspapers and in government publications are examples of
questions.explanation: They come from outside the organisation.

questions.stem: The protection of information against unauthorised access, change or loss is called
questions.explanation: Information security protects data from misuse or loss.

questions.stem: Too much information arriving at once, making it difficult for a manager to decide, is known as
questions.explanation: Overload hinders decision-making.

questions.stem:
Case study: Halima has just been employed as a receptionist at Arewa Plastics Ltd, Kaduna. On her first day, a visitor arrives without an appointment demanding to see the Managing Director, the telephone rings continually, a courier delivers a parcel for the Sales Manager, and two job applicants wait for interviews while the Personnel Manager is late. Halima leaves the desk unattended for twenty minutes to look for the Sales Manager.
(a) Identify two mistakes Halima made. [4 marks]
(b) Explain how Halima should have handled the visitor without an appointment. [4 marks]
(c) State four qualities of a good receptionist that Halima needs. [8 marks]
(d) Name two records Halima should keep at the reception desk. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: leaving the reception desk unattended for a long time
2 marks: not arranging cover / not using the telephone or intercom to reach the Sales Manager
2 marks: greet the visitor politely and take his name and business card
2 marks: explain that the MD is busy and offer an appointment or another officer, recording details
2 marks: courtesy and a pleasant manner
2 marks: patience and tact
2 marks: good telephone and communication skills
2 marks: neat appearance / discretion / good knowledge of the organisation
2 marks: visitors' (callers') register
2 marks: appointments diary / telephone message pad / staff in-out board
questions.explanation: Halima should never have left the desk unattended; she should have used the telephone or intercom or asked for relief. The visitor should be welcomed courteously, his details taken, and an appointment or another officer offered. A receptionist needs courtesy, patience, tact, good communication and discretion, and keeps a visitors' register, appointments diary and message pad.

questions.stem:
(a) Define an office. [2 marks]
(b) Explain five functions of an office. [10 marks]
(c) Give four advantages of an open-plan office. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: a place where information is received, recorded, processed, stored and communicated for the organisation
2 marks: receiving information (letters, calls, reports)
2 marks: recording information (books, files, computers)
2 marks: arranging/processing information
2 marks: giving out/communicating information
2 marks: safeguarding assets and records
2 marks: easier supervision of staff
2 marks: cheaper to build, light, heat or cool
2 marks: easy sharing of equipment and communication between staff
2 marks: flexible use of space / workflow is easy to follow
questions.explanation: An office is the place where an organisation's information is received, recorded, processed, stored and communicated. Functions include receiving, recording, arranging, giving out information and safeguarding assets. Open-plan offices allow easy supervision, lower costs, shared equipment, easy communication and flexible layout.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four departments found in a large manufacturing company. [4 marks]
(b) State two functions of each department named in (a). [8 marks]
(c) Explain the terms (i) span of control and (ii) delegation. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: production department
1 mark: sales/marketing department
1 mark: accounts department
1 mark: personnel (human resources) department
2 marks: production: manufactures goods; plans production and quality control
2 marks: sales/marketing: sells products; advertises and does market research
2 marks: accounts: keeps financial records; pays wages and bills
2 marks: personnel: recruits and trains staff; handles welfare and discipline
4 marks: span of control: the number of subordinates directly supervised by one superior, which should be manageable
4 marks: delegation: passing authority to a subordinate to carry out a task while the superior remains responsible
questions.explanation: Typical departments are production, sales/marketing, accounts and personnel (also purchasing, PR, transport). Span of control is the number of subordinates one superior directly manages; delegation is assigning authority for tasks to subordinates while retaining overall responsibility.

questions.stem:
(a) State four factors to consider when choosing office equipment. [8 marks]
(b) Explain the use of each of the following machines: (i) franking machine; (ii) shredder; (iii) photocopier; (iv) laminator. [8 marks]
(c) State two advantages of using machines in the office. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: cost of buying and running the machine
2 marks: volume and type of work to be done
2 marks: availability of after-sales service and spare parts
2 marks: space available / ease of use / staff training / safety
2 marks: franking machine: prints postage impressions on mail
2 marks: shredder: destroys confidential documents
2 marks: photocopier: makes copies of documents
2 marks: laminator: seals documents in plastic for protection
2 marks: work is done faster and more accurately
2 marks: saves labour and cost over time / produces neat work
questions.explanation: Choose equipment by cost, workload, after-sales service, space, ease of use and safety. Franking machines print postage, shredders destroy confidential papers, photocopiers reproduce documents and laminators protect documents with plastic. Machines increase speed, accuracy and neatness and reduce labour costs.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the use of each of the following documents: (i) letter of enquiry; (ii) quotation; (iii) invoice; (iv) credit note; (v) statement of account. [10 marks]
(b) Distinguish between a debit note and a credit note. [4 marks]
(c) Explain three uses of a delivery note. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: letter of enquiry: sent by a buyer asking about goods, prices and terms
2 marks: quotation: reply from seller giving prices and terms
2 marks: invoice: bill sent by seller showing goods supplied and amount due
2 marks: credit note: sent by seller to reduce the amount owed, e.g. for returns or overcharge
2 marks: statement of account: summary of transactions and balance owed at month end
2 marks: debit note increases the amount the buyer owes (undercharge)
2 marks: credit note reduces the amount the buyer owes (returns/overcharge)
2 marks: accompanies goods to show what is delivered
2 marks: checked against goods received to confirm quantity and condition
2 marks: signed by buyer as proof of delivery for the seller
questions.explanation: Letter of enquiry asks for information; a quotation answers with prices and terms; an invoice bills the buyer; a credit note reduces the debt; a statement summarises the month. Debit notes increase and credit notes reduce the amount due. Delivery notes travel with goods, allow checking and, when signed, prove delivery.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe five steps in handling incoming mail. [10 marks]
(b) Explain five services offered by the Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST) to business organisations. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: collect mail and sort private/confidential items unopened
2 marks: open other mail with a letter opener, checking that envelopes are empty
2 marks: date-stamp the letters
2 marks: check enclosures and record remittances in the remittances book
2 marks: sort and distribute to departments, recording in a mail register
2 marks: registered mail for valuable/important items
2 marks: express mail service (EMS) for fast delivery
2 marks: private mail bag / post office box
2 marks: parcel post
2 marks: poste restante / money orders / franking licence / business reply service
questions.explanation: Incoming mail is collected and sorted, private mail passed unopened, other letters opened, date-stamped, enclosures checked and remittances recorded, then sorted and distributed. NIPOST offers registered mail, EMS (speedpost), PO boxes and private mail bags, parcel post, poste restante, money orders and franking licences.

questions.stem:
(a) State four reasons why organisations file documents. [8 marks]
(b) Describe three methods of classifying files. [6 marks]
(c) State three qualities of a good filing system. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: to keep documents safe and clean
2 marks: to find documents easily when needed
2 marks: to keep records for reference and legal purposes
2 marks: to ensure confidentiality / orderliness / continuity
2 marks: alphabetical: by names of persons or firms
2 marks: numerical: by numbers with an alphabetical index
2 marks: geographical / subject / chronological with correct description
2 marks: simplicity: easy to understand and use
2 marks: accessibility and quick retrieval
2 marks: security, economy, flexibility for expansion
questions.explanation: Filing protects documents, allows quick retrieval, preserves records for reference and law and keeps confidentiality. Methods include alphabetical, numerical, geographical, subject and chronological. A good system is simple, accessible, secure, economical, compact and flexible.

questions.stem:
(a) Define communication. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the following forms of communication with an example of each: (i) upward; (ii) downward; (iii) horizontal. [6 marks]
(c) Discuss four barriers to effective communication in an office. [8 marks]
(d) State two ways of overcoming barriers to communication. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the process of sending information, ideas or messages from a sender to a receiver who understands it
2 marks: upward: from subordinates to superiors, e.g. reports, suggestions
2 marks: downward: from superiors to subordinates, e.g. instructions, memos
2 marks: horizontal: between people of the same level, e.g. departmental heads meeting
2 marks: language/jargon
2 marks: noise and physical distractions
2 marks: poor listening / attitude / emotions
2 marks: wrong choice of medium / distance / faulty equipment
2 marks: use simple clear language and the right medium
2 marks: encourage feedback / reduce noise / train staff in listening
questions.explanation: Communication transfers a message so that it is understood. Upward goes from junior to senior, downward from senior to junior, horizontal between equals. Barriers include jargon, noise, poor listening, emotions, wrong media and faulty equipment. Overcome them with clear language, the right medium, feedback and a good environment.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following terms used in meetings: (i) agenda; (ii) quorum; (iii) motion; (iv) minutes; (v) adjournment. [10 marks]
(b) State five duties of a secretary before and during a meeting. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: agenda: list of items to be discussed in order
2 marks: quorum: minimum number of members required for a valid meeting
2 marks: motion: a formal proposal put before the meeting for debate and decision
2 marks: minutes: official written record of the proceedings and decisions
2 marks: adjournment: postponing or suspending a meeting to a later time
2 marks: prepares and sends out the notice and agenda
2 marks: books the venue and arranges seating and materials
2 marks: reads the minutes of the last meeting
2 marks: takes notes of proceedings and records attendance
2 marks: assists the chairman with documents / handles correspondence
questions.explanation: Agenda lists the business; quorum is the minimum attendance; a motion is a formal proposal; minutes record proceedings; adjournment postpones the meeting. The secretary issues notices and agenda, prepares the venue, reads previous minutes, records proceedings and attendance and supports the chairman.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a report? [2 marks]
(b) Name and explain five parts of a formal report. [10 marks]
(c) State four qualities of a good report. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: a formal written or oral presentation of facts, findings and recommendations on a matter
2 marks: title: indicates the subject of the report
2 marks: terms of reference: what the writer was asked to do
2 marks: introduction / procedure: background and methods used
2 marks: findings: facts discovered
2 marks: conclusions and recommendations / appendix / signature and date
2 marks: accuracy
2 marks: objectivity / impartiality
2 marks: clarity and logical arrangement
2 marks: conciseness / timeliness
questions.explanation: A report is a formal presentation of facts and findings. Parts include title, terms of reference, introduction/procedure, findings, conclusions, recommendations, appendices and signature with date. Good reports are accurate, objective, clear, concise, well arranged and timely.
